course_description: This course provides comprehensive instruction in the assessment and management of acquired communication and swallowing disorders in adults. Students explore psycholinguistic models of language processing and develop specialised skills in assessing and treating aphasia across all modalities including spoken word processing and production, reading/dyslexia, writing/dysgraphia, and sentence-level comprehension and production. The course covers evidence-based approaches to adults with dementia and its subtypes, neurodegenerative conditions, and head and neck cancer, while also addressing service delivery in specialised contexts such as residential aged care facilities and palliative care settings. Through in-person tutorials, pre-recorded lectures, and practical activities, students develop critical thinking skills for clinical reasoning, learn to integrate research evidence into practice, and build competencies for person-centred care with older adults and their families across a range of clinical settings.

course_aims: This course aims to develop students' expertise in the assessment and management of acquired communication and swallowing disorders in adults. Students will develop advanced clinical reasoning skills through authentic case-based learning activities, building their ability to assess, differentially diagnose, and devise person- and family-centred speech pathology management plans. The course focuses on developing competencies in monitoring and evaluating progress of individual treatment goals and modifying evidence-based interventions to meet changing client needs. Students will gain an understanding of interprofessional collaboration in the management of adults with communication and swallowing disorders across diverse healthcare settings. Through a combination of pre-recorded lectures and interactive tutorials, students will engage in independent, small group, and large group inquiry-based/ practical learning activities that foster critical thinking and evidence-based practice in the specialised area of acquired neurological communication disorders and oncological conditions. Although this flipped approach to learning provides students with more flexibility, the associated workload is similar to that of a traditional course.

learning_outcomes.description: Explain the impact of aging and common age-related health conditions on communication and swallowing abilities in older adults. (SPA PS 1.1, 1.3, 1.6, 1.7, 3.1, 3.2).
Apply appropriate assessment tools and protocols to evaluate communication and swallowing disorders in adults across different clinical contexts (SPA PS 1.5, 3.2, 3.3).

Demonstrate understanding of evidence-based intervention approaches for managing communication and swallowing disorders across a range of populations, including stroke and neurodegenerative disease (SPA PS 1.1, 1.3, 3.4, 3.5).
Identify the principles of person and family-centred care when working with adults and their support networks in various healthcare settings (SPA PS 1.4, 1.6, 3.4).

Recognise the psychosocial impact of communication and swallowing disorders in adults and apply appropriate counselling strategies within the scope of speech pathology practice (SPA PS 1.4, 3.4, 3.5).
Discuss ethical considerations in providing speech pathology services within different populations and contexts, including in palliative care (SPA PS 1.1, 1.2, 1.6).

assessment_details.task_description: There will be a series of five (5) weekly knowledge check quizzes in this course, which will be comprised of multiple choice questions. Your three (3) highest scoring quizzes will make up your 10% grade (i.e., each quiz will contribute equally, with your total percentage correct from the 3 highest quizzes being used to calculate the 10% weighting). The two (2) quizzes that you receive the lowest marks for (which may include any quizzes that are not submitted or are submitted late) will not contribute to your grade. Quizzes will cover content from weeks 2-6. Each quiz opens during the content week but is due the following Monday at 1pm (e.g., the Week 2 quiz opens in Week 2 and is due Monday of Week 3 by 1pm). learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From O-week To Week 13 (20 Jul - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Online self-directed learning Pre-recorded lectures providing preparatory information will be released in O week for student viewing prior to commencement of the course. Specifically, these lectures will provide an overview of the course and associated assessment, as well as an introduction to aphasia, psycholinguistics and cognitive neuropsychology. Pre-recorded lecture content will also be available on blackboard across weeks 2-13. It is expected that students will engage with this content prior to attending the weekly tutorials.
Lectures An on campus face to face 2-hour lecture will be provided in week 1 of semester introducing a psycholinguistic model of language processing.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 2 To Week 13 (03 Aug - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Weekly on-campus Tutorials Weekly 2-hour tutorials will be held in weeks 2-6 and 8-13 of semester. Tutorials will be practically-based and will facilitate student understanding and application of the course content.
